perfect.label: Perfect rhyme
perfect.explain: Everything from the stressed vowel onwards matches exactly.

accent.label: Sound rhyme
accent.explain: Rhymes out loud even if the spelling says no: the r after a vowel goes quiet.

slant.label: Slant rhyme
slant.explain: The vowels match and the consonants are close. Most great flows run on these.

multi.label: Multi
multi.explain: Two or more syllables rhyme in a row. This is what makes a crowd react.

dialect.label: Slang rhyme
dialect.explain: Rhymes on how people actually talk, like 'thing' said as 'ting'.

cheap.label: Cheap rhyme
cheap.explain: Easy and predictable. Good for warming up, but go for something rarer.

chains.note: Say them out loud: the r in 'farmer' and 'armour' goes quiet, so they land right on 'drama'.

words.def: Exciting, emotional events, or a play for stage or screen.
The idea that what you put out comes back to you.
Protective metal covering worn in battle.
Someone who wins people over easily.
A long-necked South American animal, related to the camel.
Over-the-top emotion, like a soap opera.
A wide, unbroken view of a whole area.
words.ex: Top floor of the block, I'm taking in the panorama

words.def: In Hindu and Buddhist thought, your true duty or path in life.
words.ex: Stay on my dharma, I don't need the drama

chains.note: Out loud, 'order' sounds like 'aw-duh', a near-perfect match for 'water'. The t and d are close enough.

words.def: The clear liquid that falls as rain and fills rivers and seas.
A request for something, or things arranged neatly.
The line where one country or area ends and another begins.
A device that records sound, or a simple wooden flute.
A fan, or someone who backs you.
To kill brutally, or to beat someone heavily.
The paste that holds bricks together.
Someone who stores up far more than they need.
A raider who roams around looking for things to steal.
words.ex: Roll through the ends like a marauder, no order

chains.note: A multi: three syllables rhyme in a row (ID-ee-un). Long words like these sound clever because the whole tail of the word matches.

words.def: A phrase whose meaning isn't literal, like 'spill the tea'.
Everyday, ordinary, part of daily life.
words.ex: Bars are quotidian, I spit 'em like it's every day, see

words.def: Shiny black glass formed when lava cools fast.
words.ex: Cold heart, black ice, mind sharp like obsidian

words.def: An imaginary line from pole to pole; also the peak of something.
words.ex: Greenwich meridian, I'm the line that the time's on

words.def: Harmful in a slow, sneaky way you don't notice at first.
words.ex: Doubt is insidious, creeps in like it's hideous
Perfidious man, you'd sell your mates for a video

words.def: Very fussy about details and doing things properly.
words.ex: Fastidious with the flow, every syllable placed

words.def: Unfair, and likely to cause resentment.
words.ex: Comparing me to them? That's invidious, bro
Viridian waves when the beat goes oceanic

chains.note: Assonance: the vowels match (AN-uh) and the consonants just sit close. It's about sound, not spelling, and it's what most great flows run on.

words.def: Happening without a plan or pattern.
A song people sing together with pride.
A group of guys; your friends (slang).
Money demanded to free someone held captive.
A ghost, or something that isn't really there.
Two things working together, side by side.
All the fans of something, as a community.
Biased information spread to push a point of view.

words.ex: Speak with candour, no propaganda

words.def: A written note, often an official record or agreement.
words.ex: Sign the memorandum, me and the mandem

chains.note: Said casually, 'thing' becomes 'ting'. Freestylers rhyme on how they actually talk, not how it's written.

words.def: An object, or a matter or situation.
A circle, often jewellery worn on a finger.
A male ruler of a country.
The season after winter, or a coiled bit of metal.
A toy, or someone treated like one.
A rich, never-ending source of something.
words.ex: My mind's a wellspring, every bar's a new ting
You're an underling, I'm the one that crowned the king

chains.note: The easiest rhyme in English. Fine for warming up, but crowds hear '-ation' coming. Try landing a rarer word instead.

words.def: A place where trains or buses stop.
Feeling annoyed because you can't do something.
The ability to picture things in your mind.
Putting off things you should do now.
Nervous fear about something coming up.
words.ex: Step to the mic with no trepidation
Give the OGs veneration
Bars spread like a conflagration

words.def: Giving up something you want, often for others.
words.ex: Self-abnegation, I give it all to the station

words.def: Being deliberately vague to avoid committing.
words.ex: Straight talk, no equivocation

chains.note: Match the stressed vowel (ED), then let '-uh-bul' carry the rest. 'Impeccable' still works because 'EK' is close to 'ED'.

words.def: To do with medicine and health.
So memorable you can't forget it.
Unfortunate; something you'd wish hadn't happened.

words.ex: Ink on the page is indelible

words.def: Too great or intense to put into words.
words.ex: The feeling's ineffable, flow's incredible
Timing's impeccable, every bar's edible

chains.note: A clean perfect rhyme, but the advanced words are where the points are. 'Erudition' beats 'mission' every time.

words.def: Sight, or a clear idea of the future.
A custom passed down through generations.
A belief in luck or magic without evidence.
Deep knowledge from lots of study.
words.ex: Pure erudition, I study the vision
War of attrition, I outlast the competition

words.def: Speech or action stirring up rebellion against the state.
words.ex: They call it sedition, I call it my mission

words.def: A feeling that something's about to happen.
words.ex: Had a premonition I'd win this position

chains.note: Three syllables to match: the stressed vowel, then 'ee-us'. 'Curious' and 'serious' have slightly different vowels but ride together fine.

words.def: Wanting to know or learn things.
Confused and wild, from illness or excitement.
Bossy and arrogant, acting like a ruler.
words.ex: Imperious, I rule the room, I'm serious

words.def: Fake, or based on bad reasoning.
words.ex: Your claims are spurious, that's why I'm furious
Penurious past but the future's luxurious
Bars injurious, keep it curious

chains.note: 'Pocket' and 'topic' don't match on paper, but say them quickly and they're close. Mosaic rhymes like 'stop it' use two words to match one.

words.def: A small pouch sewn into clothes.
A vehicle that flies into space.
Let it fall, or release something new.
The hot region either side of the equator.
Too small to see without a microscope.

words.ex: Your view's myopic, I see past the topic
Philanthropic with the bars, take one for your pocket
Misanthropic mood, so I'm leaving in a rocket
Flow's kaleidoscopic, every bar a new topic

chains.note: Perfect rhyme on 'EN-tul'. Long words ending in '-mental' let you stack three or four syllables of rhyme.

words.def: To do with the mind; also slang for crazy.
Something you pay to use for a while.

words.ex: Doubting me's detrimental, my flow's monumental
Transcendental on the instrumental
Fame's incidental, the bars are fundamental

chains.note: A goldmine of advanced vocab. Every one of these ends in 'ISH-us', so once you find the vowel the rhyme is free.

words.def: A good sign that things will go well.
words.ex: Auspicious start, the beat's delicious
Capricious crowd, so my flow stays vicious
Avaricious? Nah, I'm just ambitious
Expeditious with the bars, no time to be suspicious

words.def: Done secretly so no one notices.
words.ex: Surreptitious, slid in quiet, now I'm vicious

chains.note: Three-syllable multi. Get the 'AIR' sound right and four words in a row will sound planned.

words.def: A star sign, the water carrier.

words.ex: Nefarious plans, but the bars are hilarious
Your position's precarious
Gregarious, I'm with the mandem in various
Live vicarious through my bars, it's hilarious

chains.note: Mixing 'subtle', 'trouble' and 'struggle' works because the vowel (UH) is identical. The middle consonant can change.

words.def: A ball of air in liquid.
To handle several things at once.
Broken stone from a ruined building.

words.ex: Here's my rebuttal, it's subtle but it's trouble
Wordplay to befuddle, leave 'em in a muddle

chains.note: One-syllable perfect rhymes are easy to hit, so use them to land the end of a line hard.

words.def: Words that end with the same sound.
A comic Christmas stage show where the audience shouts along.
A model or way of seeing things.
words.ex: Shift the paradigm every time I rhyme

words.def: To do with the sea and ships.
words.ex: Maritime flow, I'm sailing through time

chains.note: Three syllables, stress on the first. 'Battery' and 'flattery' swap AL for AT, and the ear still accepts it.

words.def: Pay you get for a job.
A unit of energy in food.
A mistaken belief or faulty argument.
words.ex: Your flow's a fallacy, mine's from a galaxy
Turn words into gold, call it alchemy

chains.note: Four syllables matching (OK-ruh-see). 'Philosophy' only partly fits, but the rhythm sells it.

words.def: Total control of a market; also a board game.
The study of big questions about life.
A system weighed down by officials and rules.
words.ex: Cut the bureaucracy, skip the hypocrisy

words.def: Rule by one person with total power.
words.ex: Mic's my autocracy, no democracy
Not born in the aristocracy

words.def: A system where people rise by ability.
words.ex: Freestyle's a meritocracy

words.def: A state ruled by religious leaders.
words.ex: Mic is my church, call it theocracy

chains.note: Out loud, 'caught' and 'court' can sound identical, because the r goes quiet. Spelling hides rhymes like this.

words.def: Showed someone how to do something.
Where trials happen, or where you play tennis.

words.ex: Fraught with nerves but I'm never caught short
Left 'em distraught with a single thought

words.def: A huge, unstoppable force; also a big lorry.
words.ex: Juggernaut flow, can't be stopped or caught
Bar onslaught, every line's taught

chains.note: 'Saw', 'sore' and 'soar' can all sound the same out loud. That opens up hundreds of extra rhymes.

words.def: Looked at; or a cutting tool.
An extra performance because the crowd wants more.
A close, easy connection with people.
words.ex: Got rapport with the crowd, they're screaming for more
Fake MCs I abhor, keep it raw

chains.note: 'Star', 'spa' and 'memoir' all end on the same open 'ah', so French borrowings fit right in.

words.def: A burning sun far away; or a famous person.
A line of rap; or a place to drink.
An icon or character that represents you.
A market with lots of stalls.
A book of someone's own memories.
words.ex: Every bar's a page of my memoir

words.def: The full range of things someone can perform.
words.ex: Deep repertoire, I'm a star
Biting my flow? That's a faux pas

chains.note: Perfect rhyme. Advanced words add weight, because 'retribution' hits harder than 'solution'.

words.def: Dirt and poison in the environment.
A country's founding rules; or your health.

words.ex: Bars are retribution
No absolution, this is evolution

words.def: The breaking up or ending of something.
words.ex: Dissolution of your crew, that's the solution

words.def: Paying back for something lost or stolen.
words.ex: Want restitution for the bars you took

chains.note: Mosaic rhyme: 'flipped it' (two words) rhymes with 'cryptic' (one word). Splitting a rhyme across words is a key freestyle skill.

words.def: Turned it over; changed it up.
Like the end of the world.
words.ex: Apocalyptic flow, I didn't script it
Three bars, a triptych, cryptic

chains.note: Perfect rhyme. All adjectives, so you can describe yourself or your opponent in a chain.

words.def: Harsh and controlling; or heavy and stifling.
words.ex: Heat's oppressive, flow's impressive
Transgressive bars, a bit aggressive

chains.note: 'Pretentious' adds 'us' but keeps the EN-shun core. A slightly longer word still counts.

words.def: A measurement; or a whole other world.
Trying to seem more important than you are.

words.ex: Contentious bars, I get attention
Apprehension, you can feel the tension
Your condescension, I don't even mention

chains.note: Single-syllable punch. Words like 'matriarch' put the rhyme on a syllable that isn't stressed, which gives a cool off-beat feel.

words.def: A bit of fun; also a songbird.
A woman who heads a family or group.
words.ex: Nan's the matriarch, she lit the spark

words.def: A man who heads a family or group.
words.ex: Patriarch talk, but you're a lark

words.def: One of a small group of rich, powerful people.
words.ex: Flow like an oligarch, money in the dark

chains.note: Perfect rhyme. Advanced verbs like 'curtail' and 'regale' make your bars sound deliberate.

words.def: Size or level; or a fish's skin plate.

words.ex: I regale 'em with a tale
Try to curtail me, I prevail
Assail the mic, I never fail

chains.note: Hugely common rhyme sound. Reach for 'erudite' or 'contrite' to stand out.

words.ex: Erudite, I read all night
Not contrite, I'm right
Your bars are trite, mine are dynamite

chains.note: 'Contagious' and 'tenacious' differ on one consonant (j vs sh), which is close enough. A crowd hears the vowel.

words.ex: Audacious, contagious, flow's outrageous
Tenacious, I'm courageous
Loquacious, I talk 'til the room's spacious
Vivacious crowd, the energy's contagious
Sagacious with the bars, gracious
Home crowd's advantageous

chains.note: Say 'khaki' as 'KAH-kee' and it lands on 'snarky'. How you pronounce a word can unlock a rhyme.

words.def: Rule by a king or queen.
A ranking from top to bottom.

words.ex: None of that malarkey, khaki

words.def: Rule by a small, powerful group.
words.ex: Break the oligarchy, bring anarchy

chains.note: Perfect rhyme. Note 'august' (an adjective with stress on the second syllable) versus 'August' the month.

words.ex: August company, I earned their trust
Wanderlust, leave the haters in the dust

chains.note: Perfect rhyme with some brilliant vocab. 'Rigmarole' is a great word to drop.

words.def: An aim; or scoring in football.

words.ex: Cajole the crowd, take control
Skip the rigmarole, straight to the goal

chains.note: Two syllables, stress on the first. Pairs with mosaic rhymes like 'has 'em' and 'smash 'em'.

words.def: Saying the opposite of what you mean to mock.
A deep crack in the ground; a huge gap.

words.ex: Phantasm flow, I vanish, no sarcasm

chains.note: Short and punchy. Long words ending in '-iac' put the rhyme at the very end, which makes a strong closer.

words.def: A yearly book of facts and dates.
words.ex: Write my name in the almanac
Bars so sick, I'm a hypochondriac

chains.note: Perfect rhyme. 'Explosion' and 'erosion' swap sh for zh, which is still close.

words.def: The ability to move from place to place.
words.ex: Pure locomotion, my flow's an ocean

chains.note: One syllable. 'Hoodwink' gives you a two-syllable word that still lands on the rhyme.

words.ex: Can't hoodwink me, I think

chains.note: Two syllables, stress on IN. 'Underpinning' rhymes on its last two syllables, which is a quiet flex.

words.def: The foundation that holds something up.
words.ex: Faith is the underpinning, that's why I'm winning

chains.note: Perfect rhyme. Compound words like 'showdown' are easy multis.

words.ex: Renown in the town, I wear the crown

chains.note: One syllable, perfect rhyme. 'Figurehead' rhymes only its final syllable, which still works on the beat.

words.def: A baked food; also slang for money.
A pure-bred horse; or a top-quality person.
A leader in name only, with no real power.
words.ex: You're a figurehead, I'm the one that's said

chains.note: Two syllables. 'Freezing' and 'squeezing' swap n for ng, and they ride along fine.
A soft multi: three syllables with a matching vowel. 'General' and 'several' fit even though spelling differs.

words.def: Broad, not specific; or an army leader.
More than two but not many.
To do with a central government.

words.ex: Fame's ephemeral, bars are general
